description: We’re BUBLIKI, a curious team passionate about data analytics, statistics, machine learning, and software development. We love turning data into creative solutions for space exploration. We’re looking for teammates skilled in Python/R, ML, data science, web development, UI/UX, or space science. Curious learners and collaborative problem-solvers are welcome. Let’s build something out of this world!
summary: Asclepius is an explainable health expert system for astronauts on long missions, where the flight surgeon can be minutes away or out of contact behind the Moon. Every day the crew fills in a short morning and evening check-in: vitals, sleep, symptoms, mood, reaction time. The app also reads cabin CO2 and radiation dose. It compares each value with the astronaut's own six-month pre-flight baseline, not with population averages, and runs transparent IF-THEN rules built from NASA's medical knowledge, covering all 100 conditions of NASA's Integrated Medical Model plus 15 more from HRP evidence. The result is a hypothesis with a confidence level, an urgency color (green, yellow, orange, red), a "Why?" chain that names the rule and its NASA source, the steps to take now and the next measurement to make. On red it prepares a compact flight-surgeon packet and queues it while there is no link. Astronaut health records are not public, so instead of training an AI on data we do not have, we built clear rules and tested them on real data, including real Inspiration4 crew lab results from NASA OSDR.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Asclepius helps astronauts assess their own health when the flight surgeon is far away: up to 20 minutes of delay on the way to Mars, or no link at all behind the Moon. The crew fills in a short morning and evening check-in (vitals, sleep, sleepiness, symptoms, mood, reaction time, workload, food and fluid). The app adds mission context: cabin CO2, radiation dose, communication delay. It returns hypotheses with a confidence level, an urgency level (GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE, RED), a "Why?" chain that names each rule and its NASA source, concrete steps to take now, and the next best measurement when data is missing. On RED it builds a compact flight-surgeon packet; with a long delay or no link it puts onboard steps first and queues the packet until the link returns.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Facts: the latest values are compared with the astronaut's own six-month pre-flight passport (personal baseline and range), plus streaks, 7-day counts and clinical scores (NEWS2, qSOFA).

2. Rules: 86 encoded IF-THEN rules (220+ documented in the knowledge base) fire by forward chaining; several rules for one hypothesis combine as certainty factors.

3. Safety guard: "expected adaptation to spaceflight" never hides a red flag in the same body system.

4. Missing data is never treated as normal: rules without inputs stay pending and ask for the next measurement.

5. Expected in-flight shifts from NASA evidence (for example lower blood pressure) are taken into account, so normal adaptation is not flagged as illness.

KNOWLEDGE BASE

Built from the challenge resources: NASA HRP hazards and risks (every risk is a body system), all 100 conditions of NASA's Integrated Medical Model plus 15 from HRP evidence, NASA-STD-3001 and OCHMO technical briefs for limits (CO2, radiation, sleep, behavioral health, bone, workload), Human Research Roadmap evidence reports, NASA Standard Measures for the pre-flight schedule, and the CSA radiation monitoring article. 115 conditions, 102 actions, 131 references; every rule cites its source.

DATA

No public time series of astronaut vital signs exist, so each fictional crew member's six-month pre-flight passport is built from real donors: real Inspiration4 astronaut labs and microbiome data (NASA OSDR OSD-569, OSD-575, OSD-572), NHANES exams, LifeSnaps wearable streams, MMASH hormones, PTB-XL ECGs, PhysioNet tilt tests; NASA DONKI and NOAA solar events and MSL RAD dose rates for radiation. Every value carries a provenance label (real-astronaut, real-ground, real-population, synthetic-calibrated, authored).

VALIDATION ON REAL DATA

- Healthy volunteers (LifeSnaps, 23 people, 1,276 days): 92% GREEN, 0 RED.

- Real astronaut lab draws (Inspiration4, 28 draws): 4 trigger the glucose rules, flagged for flight-surgeon review.

- Emergency patients, triage vitals only (MIMIC-IV-ED demo): 27% of urgent patients escalated from vitals alone.

- Orthostatic criteria on healthy controls (PhysioNet tilt): 0 false positives.

- Radiation biodosimetry from blood gene expression (NASA OSDR OSD-410): exposure detected in 84% of samples.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Crews get explainable, source-backed guidance when Earth cannot answer in time; flight surgeons get a short, structured packet instead of raw data. Because every decision is a readable rule with a citation, the system can be reviewed, corrected and certified, which a black-box model cannot offer for medical use.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Instead of training AI on astronaut data that is not public, we turned NASA's own medical knowledge into transparent rules, the approach NASA itself pioneered with the CLIPS expert-system tool. Each astronaut is compared with their own six-month baseline, and the app adapts to communication delay and loss of signal.

TOOLS AND LANGUAGES

Python (FastAPI, Pydantic, pandas, PyYAML, pytest; 166 automated tests), TypeScript, React 18, Vite, Recharts. Deployed on a Linux server with nginx and systemd. Live demo: https://asclepius.phronesisco.tech

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Safety (decision support for self-assessment, not a diagnosis; no drug doses, medication always defers to the onboard checklist), honest handling of missing data, communication delay, privacy (a user's own crew data stays in their browser; nothing is stored on the server), no real astronaut is identified (the demo mission Hygieia I and its crew are fictional), readability (Atkinson Hyperlegible font; urgency shown by color, shape and text), and clear labelling of every synthetic value.
